To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
CTLs activated by dendritic cells loaded with prostate cancer antigen and PEP peptide exert a remarkable cytotoxicity against prostate cancer cells in vitro.
DCs loaded with the freeze-thaw antigens and PEP- 3 peptide could activate CTLs and exert cytotoxicity against the TRAMP-C2 cancer cells in vitro.

DCs loaded with both freeze- thaw antigen from prostate cancer cells and the PEP-3 epitope peptide from the TRPM1 gene can induce CTLs with strong cytotoxic effects against prostate cancer cells in vitro.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new strategy to treat prostate cancer.
the development of a novel immunotherapy for prostate cancer.
the development of a DC-based vaccine against prostate cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the DCs loaded with the TRAMP-C2 antigen and PEP3 peptide can induce the specific immune response in vitro.
CTLs activated by the DCs loaded with the freeze-thaw TRAMP-C2 antigen and PEP3 peptide could exert more evident cytotoxic effect against TRAMP-C1 cells in vitro.
the CTLs induced by DCs loaded freeze-thaw antigen of TRAMP-C2 and PEP-33 peptide could be used as a novel immunotherapeutic strategy for the prevention and treatment of prostate cancer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
DCs loaded with both freeze-thaw antigen of TRAMP-C2 and PEP- 3 peptide can be used for immunotherapy of prostate cancer.
DCs loaded with both the freeze-thaw antigens and PEP- 3 peptide are a promising strategy for the treatment of prostate cancer.
DCs loaded with both antigen and peptide are more efficient in activating CTLs against TRAMP-C1 cells than the antigen-loaded DCs or peptide-loaded DCs alone.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CTLs generated by DCs loaded freeze-thaw antigen of tumor cells and PEP- 3 peptide can be a novel immunotherapeutic strategy against prostate cancer.
the CTLs induced by DCs loaded freeze-thaw antigen of TRAMP-C2 and PEP- 3 peptide may have a great potential in the treatment of prostate cancer in the future.
DCs loaded with both freeze-thaw antigen of TRAMP-C2 and PEP-1-3 peptide could induce CTLs with higher killing efficiency against TRAM-C2 cells.
